quote: 3.6 Expenses and Invoicing. Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, each Party shall bear all costs and expenses associated with the Development activities for which such Party is responsible under this Agreement and the Initial Development Plan
rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty, or volume cap on AbbVie (our party), so it sits at the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "shortfall", "commit to purchase", "purchase" and "supply" return no commitment language: the only "minimum" references are insurance limits (Sections 11.6.1(b)-(c)), and there is no obligation for AbbVie to buy any quantity of Licensed Compound or Product from Harpoon. To the contrary, Section 4.5.1 gives AbbVie "the sole right, at its expense, to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply the Licensed Compound and Licensed Products for commercial sale," with a manufacturing technology transfer available on AbbVie's request (Section 4.5.2), so supply volumes are entirely at our election. AbbVie's payment obligations are the Section 6.1 upfront fee and success-based development/regulatory milestones and royalties on Net Sales (Sections 6.2-6.3), which are event- and usage-linked rather than guaranteed minimum spend, and Section 3.6 allocates development costs to the responsible Party rather than committing AbbVie to a floor. Section 4.2 is a Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence covenant, not a volume commitment, and remedies are limited to a good-faith discussion process. Nothing to redline for this rule; commitments running from Harpoon to us are outside the rule's scope.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that the finding proposes no redline and no counterparty comment — the paragraphs are returned unchanged, which is the expected output for a compliant classification. The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 4.5.1 gives AbbVie the sole right (not obligation) to Manufacture and supply, Section 6.2 payments are event-triggered milestones, and Section 3.6 allocates development costs per responsible Party — none is a minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap on Customer. Rationale correctly notes the rule's scope limit (commitments running from Harpoon to us are out of scope) and correctly treats the only 'minimum' hits (insurance limits) as irrelevant, so the clause sits at the preferred position rather than merely the fallback. No deterministic check failures and no over-flagging risk, since nothing is being raised as a negotiation issue; the finding functions only as internal evidence.

quote: 10.4 Covenants of AbbVie. AbbVie covenants to Harpoon as follows:
rationale: Searches for "solicit", "induce", "hire" and "employ" across the Agreement return no employee non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant. AbbVie's only affirmative covenant (Section 10.4.1) concerns obtaining IP/confidentiality rights from its personnel, and the miscellaneous article (Section 13) contains only force majeure and Harpoon change-of-control provisions. The nearest employee-related provision, Section 6.15 (No Other Compensation), merely confirms that no side payments have been made to the other Party's employees in connection with the transaction; it does not restrict hiring or solicitation. The Agreement therefore imposes no non-solicit on us, which is the playbook's preferred position, so no redline is required.

quote: 12.1.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated in accordance herewith, shall continue in force and effect until (a) the date of expiration of the last Royalty Term for the last Licensed Product, or (b) the expiration of the License Option Period and the failure of AbbVie to exercise the License Option (such period, the "Term").
rationale: Section 12.1.1 fixes a definite Term running to expiry of the last Royalty Term (or lapse of the License Option Period) with no evergreen or auto-renewal mechanic; searches for "renew"/"automatically" return no renewal, non-renewal notice window, or renewal price-uplift language anywhere in the Agreement. Any extension would therefore require a mutual written amendment under Section 13.9, which matches the playbook's preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement). There is no notice window to shorten and no uplift to cap, so no redline is warranted; on expiry Section 12.1.2 actually converts our licence to a fully-paid, royalty-free, irrevocable grant, which is favourable to us.

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 12.1.1 sets a definite Term ending at expiry of the last Royalty Term or lapse of the License Option Period, with no evergreen/auto-renewal mechanic, non-renewal notice window, or renewal price-uplift language. Absence of auto-renewal means any extension requires a mutual written amendment, which matches the playbook's preferred position ('renewal only by mutual written agreement'), so no redline or counterparty comment is expected — and none was proposed (redline is byte-identical to the original). The failed deterministic check ('non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days: number not found') is expected here, since there is no notice window to measure; it does not indicate a defect in the finding. quote: 3.8.4 Compliance. Each Party shall perform or cause to be performed, any and all of its Development activities, including Initial Development Activities, in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law.
rationale: This is a development and option/licence agreement rather than a services or software contract, so the rule maps to Harpoon's performance and quality warranties. Harpoon stands behind its work at or above the preferred position: (a) Section 3.8.4 requires all Development activities (including the Initial Development Activities Harpoon performs) to be conducted "in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law" - the industry equivalent of "professional and workmanlike" plus the compliance-with-laws warranty; (b) Section 10.3.3 obliges Harpoon to employ personnel with appropriate knowledge, expertise and experience for those activities; and (c) Section 10.2 gives an extensive Harpoon-only warranty set (IP ownership and non-infringement, in-licence compliance, accuracy and completeness of Regulatory Documentation and Know-How including materials made available after the Effective Date under 10.2.11, no untrue FDA statements, and no debarment with an express AbbVie termination right under 10.2.14). Duration comfortably exceeds the preferred 12 months: the Section 3.8.4 and 10.3 obligations run for the whole Term rather than a 90-day or 12-month conformance window. The disclaimer in Section 10.5 does not swallow the express warranties - it is mutual and opens "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so it reaches only implied warranties and is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away. No malicious-code warranty is needed as no software is delivered. The only sub-element short of the model language is the absence of an express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence; that mechanic is not apt for a clinical development collaboration, where the remedy is Harpoon's Section 11.2 indemnity, damages, and AbbVie's termination rights for material breach (including the notice-and-discussion process in Section 3.1.2). We note this rather than flagging it.

checks.name: warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and the finding correctly produces no redline and no counterparty comment — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, so nothing invalid or directionally wrong is proposed. The cited text supports compliance as mapped to this document type (a pharma development and option agreement): Section 3.8.4 supplies the 'good scientific manner' / compliance-with-Applicable-Law equivalent of the professional-and-workmanlike plus legal-compliance warranty, Section 10.3.3 adds a personnel-competence undertaking, and Section 10.2 contains an extensive Harpoon-only warranty set (IP, in-licence, accuracy of Regulatory Documentation/Know-How, no untrue FDA statements, no debarment with an AbbVie termination right). The disclaimer in Section 10.5 opens with 'EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN' and is mutual, so it reaches only implied warranties and does not swallow the express warranties — the clause is nowhere near the 'AS IS' walk-away position. The failed deterministic check (no 90-day/months warranty period) is a phrasing/context artefact rather than a substantive gap: the Section 3.8.4 and 10.3 obligations and the Section 10.2 warranties operate across the Term, which exceeds the preferred 12-month/90-day windows, and no software or deliverable conformance window exists to measure. The only shortfall — no express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence — is a sub-element correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with playbook classification semantics; remedies here run through the Section 11.2 indemnity and material-breach termination rights, and no malicious-code warranty is apt since no software is delivered.

quote: 11.6 Insurance. Each Party shall obtain and carry in full force and effect the minimum insurance requirements set forth herein. Such insurance (a) shall be primary insurance with respect to each Party's own participation under this Agreement, (b) shall be issued by a recognized insurer rated by A.M. Best "A-VII" (or its equivalent) or better, or an insurer pre- approved in writing by the other Party, and (c) shall list the other Party as an additional insured under the General Liability Policy.
rationale: Section 11.6 contains a usable insurance clause binding each Party (including Harpoon): general liability insurance with per-occurrence and aggregate limits including clinical trial coverage (11.6.1(c)), workers' compensation at statutory limits and employer's liability where it has U.S. employees (11.6.1(a)-(b)), certificates of insurance on request plus claims-made tail coverage (11.6.2), and A.M. Best-rated insurers with AbbVie named as additional insured. That matches the structure of the preferred position on the material terms for this development/option collaboration. No professional (E&O) or cyber/privacy layer is specified, but Harpoon is a co-development partner that does not host or process Customer Data or work on our premises, so those limits are not engaged; the specific dollar limits are redacted ([***]) and should be confirmed commercially. Section 11.6.3 preserves AbbVie's right to self-insure, which benefits us. No redline warranted.

verification.notes: The rule is a 'missing'-kind check for the presence of a vendor insurance clause; Section 11.6 supplies a usable, mutual insurance regime (workers' comp at statutory limits, employer's liability, general liability with per-occurrence and aggregate limits including clinical trial coverage, A.M. Best-rated insurers, additional insured status, and certificates on request plus claims-made tail), so the compliant classification is supported by the cited text. No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed — consistent with the claimed status and with the deterministic check ('insurance obligation present' = ok). The absence of an E&O and cyber/privacy layer is correctly treated as a sub-element noted in the rationale rather than a deviation: this is a development/option collaboration in which the counterparty is not hosting or processing Customer Data or working on our premises, so the walk-away trigger (no insurance for a data-processing/on-premises vendor) is not engaged. Section 11.6.3 (AbbVie self-insurance right) benefits our party, so it is properly not flagged; the rationale appropriately flags the redacted [***] limits for commercial confirmation rather than asserting compliance with specific dollar thresholds.

quote: (a) as soon as reasonably practicable, destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of the other Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party; or (b) as soon as reasonably practicable, deliver to the requesting Party, at such other Party's expense, all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of such other Party
rationale: The Agreement contains usable exit machinery covering both limbs of this rule, and the direction favours us on the data limb. Section 9.7 (p0517–p0518) is a mutual, termination-triggered return-or-destroy right exercisable at the requesting Party's written election, with written certification of destruction where deletion is chosen, and it expressly limits the other Party's retention to one archival/legal-compliance copy plus automated back-ups — that is the preferred "return, then delete and certify" construct, applied in our favour against Harpoon as well as against us. The wind-down/transition limb is covered by Section 12.6.1(c) and Article 12.7 (reversion of Harpoon Reversion Products, transfer of Regulatory Documentation and data, and AbbVie assistance as Harpoon reasonably requests), by the post-termination sell-off period in Section 12.10.2, and by surviving Section 3.8.5 (p0331), which continues Harpoon's record-retention and AbbVie's right to copies after termination. Note also that Harpoon's forward-looking transfer and assistance obligations sit in Sections 3.5, 3.8.2(a) and 4.5.2 (full Manufacturing Technology Transfer with reasonable assistance, continuing at AbbVie's request against reimbursement) — the "help moving" that this rule protects is already ours. Direction check: the exit transfer/destruction obligations in Article 12.7 and Section 12.6.1(c) run from AbbVie to Harpoon because rights in the Licensed Compounds revert to Harpoon on termination; that is inherent in the option/licence bargain, not a vendor-side gap, and inserting a Vendor data-return clause would be inapposite since Harpoon holds no AbbVie-owned service data as a processor. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: Section 9.7 uses "as soon as reasonably practicable" instead of a fixed thirty-day export window, and specifies no machine-readable format; and Section 12.6.1(c) lets Harpoon elect destruction of AbbVie-generated data (though Section 12.10.2's sell-off period and Section 9.7's retained archival copy blunt this, and it is not immediate deletion of our own data). On its material terms the clause set meets the fallback and substantially the preferred position, so no redline.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is a no-op with no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing improper is being proposed to the counterparty. The cited text supports compliance on the data limb: Section 9.7 (p0517–p0518) is a termination-triggered, mutual return-or-destroy right at the requesting Party's written election, with written certification of destruction and retention limited to one archival/legal copy plus automated back-ups. That is the rule's 'return, then delete and certify' construct and is well clear of the walk-away ('no data return, or immediate deletion'). The transition limb is addressed with real cites (Article 12.7 reversion, Section 12.6.1(c), the post-termination sell-off window in 12.10.2, surviving record/copy rights in 3.8.5, and the forward-looking Manufacturing Technology Transfer with assistance in 3.5/3.8.2(a)/4.5.2). The direction analysis is sound: on termination rights in the Licensed Compounds revert to Harpoon, so post-termination assistance necessarily runs from AbbVie to Harpoon; inserting a Vendor-side 'return Customer Data' clause would be inapposite in a development/option/licence agreement where the counterparty is not a processor of our service data. The failed deterministic 'data return/transition present' check is a phrasing-match heuristic; the agreement uses 'Return of Confidential Information', 'destroy … and confirm such destruction in writing', and reversion/technology-transfer language rather than the playbook's services/hosting vocabulary, so the regex miss is not probative here. Shortfalls versus the preferred wording are correctly noted rather than flagged: 'as soon as reasonably practicable' instead of a fixed 30-day window, no machine-readable-format requirement, and Harpoon's election to have AbbVie-generated data destroyed under 12.6.1(c). These are sub-elements short of preferred, not failures of the fallback, so no redline is the right call under the classification semantics.
